<subject>Re: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative</subject>
<body>
I believe our discussion about an additional levy for all supplier categories was regarding our projections on how the "new MSP" recovery framework might operate, not Greenfield Farms. The recovery framework is still under consideration with several possible options.

That’s how I remember it.


From: Thomas Gade on 28/05/2024 11:05 AM
To: Reyansh Krish
cc: Chakradhar Lala, Hardik D Pal, Nihal Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan 
Subject: RE: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative

I spoke with Chakradhar. I think I misunderstood the details.
</body>
<quoted>
 -----Original Message-----
From:  Krish, Reyansh  
Sent: Tuesday, 28 May 2024 10:32 AM
To: Gade, Thomas
Cc: Lala, Chakradhar; Pal, Hardik; Karan, Nihal; Nagarajan, Ekantika
Subject: RE: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative

I don’t recall Lay mentioning the increase should apply to direct farmers. We should clarify further to ensure alignment.

Best,  
Reyansh



	Thomas Gade 23/05/2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar Lala  
cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D Pal  
Subject: RE: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative


Chakradhar, Nihal, Reyansh and I were on site with Viraj Vyas last week. Nihal mentioned Viraj might think all suppliers, including direct farmers, should bear the increase you noted. Nihal? This is good from a compliance risk perspective since if all suppliers are treated equally, our direct farmers who shifted to cooperative supply cannot claim unfair treatment. Conversely, if they must pay because they reverted to cooperative sourcing, they may seek reimbursement from us. If the increase is to recover costs from the government procurement between 01/02/24-30/03/25, and direct farmers are exempt, FarmPartnerships could face significant exposure to its partners. We may need to revise our approach accordingly.  
-----Original Message-----
From:  Lala, Chakradhar  
Sent: Thursday, 23 May 2024 08:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas; Greenfield Farms, Pune; Harvest Zone, Nashik; Stoness, AgriIndia Commodities Desk; Bakhshi, Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish, Reyansh
Subject: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative


AgriIndia’s recent filing confirms that the MSP freeze of ₹6.5 per kg does not apply to direct farmers.

In hearings on AgriIndia's potential price revision for large suppliers:  
AgriIndia has proposed to allocate all retained stock to small suppliers (below 100 quintals). Large suppliers would be served by government procurement or be direct farmers. Several stakeholders have significant concerns with this. AgriIndia calculated the expected price increase under their plan as ₹2.86 per kg. If large suppliers receive a share of retained stock, the increase rises to ₹2.99 per kg. In that case, large suppliers retain an MSP adjustment (related to long-term contracts and stranded costs) which they would lose otherwise. Our role is to seek an order 1) excluding direct farmers from any increase (the proposed ₹2.86) 2) excluding them from any surcharge related to undercollection from the freeze (amount still unknown) 3) prorating the surcharge if applicable.
</quoted>
